title: Inside the Silent Dance of Heat and Gas

segments.text: What really happens when heat hits a Stirling engine?
A fixed amount of gas—air, helium or hydrogen—is heated from outside, expands, and pushes a power piston.
The linked displacer shoves the hot gas into a cooler chamber where it contracts, creating a partial vacuum that lets the piston extract more work.
The gas never leaves the cylinder, so there are no intake or exhaust flows, keeping operation almost silent.
Meanwhile the regenerator temporarily stores heat from the cooling gas and returns it on heating, boosting efficiency.
This cycle repeats, driving the engine
